faq.a: Abdulqadeer represents Arabic عَبْدُ الْقَدِير, meaning servant of the All-Powerful.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulqadeer?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and a second element.
Yes. The underlying compound is عَبْدُ الْقَدِير (ʿAbd al-Qadīr).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdulqadeer?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; al-Qadīr is related to ق د ر (q-d-r).
Abdulqadeer is a traditional Muslim personal name because it contains a compound invoking al-Qadīr, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abdulqadeer as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.q: What does Abdulqadeer mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of the All-Powerful; the compound combines عبد with al-Qadīr.
The supplied “ab-dul-qa-deer” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.q: Is Abdulqadeer a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies the name as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
